nodes.label: ADR 0001 - Record architecture decisions
nodes.rationale: Undocumented choices get re-litigated, and an agent with no record of a decision will cheerfully make a different one next session. An ADR is half a page recording what was chosen, what was rejected and why - not how to implement it. The report's technical chapter is largely assembled from them, and writing them as we go is cheaper than reconstructing them in November.

nodes.label: ADR 0002 - One PostgreSQL instance for everything
nodes.norm_label: adr 0002 - one postgresql instance for everything
nodes.rationale: The questions a household assistant answers are relational selects and aggregates, not graph traversals, and generated Cypher from a quantised local model is the highest-variance component that could sit on a live demo path. PostgreSQL 17 with pgvector holds chunks (dense plus tsvector lexical), typed facts, obligations, LangGraph state and the registry. ChromaDB was rejected for having no keyword search; a separate graph database for being a second query language and a second failure mode for no gain. It is also the stack with the deepest representation in training data, which matters when agents write most of the code.

nodes.label: ADR 0003 - PaperBrain informs the pattern, not the module
nodes.norm_label: adr 0003 - paperbrain informs the pattern, not the module
nodes.rationale: core/retrieve/ ports PaperBrain's retrieval pattern - hybrid BM25 plus dense fused with RRF, hash-based idempotent ingest, per-page OCR fallback, a refuse-to-guess grounded prompt - rebuilt against Postgres, Docling and the pinned models. Adopting it wholesale would violate ADR 0002 with a second datastore, swap in unpinned models, ship no reranker and no graph, and pull in a parallel dependency set. Designing from a blank page would throw away a validated design. The cost: PaperBrain now needs someone to keep it from silently diverging as a second unmaintained implementation.

nodes.label: ADR 0004 - Local setup can run before the assistant is ready
nodes.norm_label: adr 0004 - local setup can run before the assistant is ready
nodes.rationale: A missing database or model must be understandable to nontechnical teammates without claiming the unfinished assistant works. The launcher starts a loopback-only FastAPI diagnostic server that owns its socket, refuses a busy port and opens the browser only once started; /readyz returns 503 throughout the setup stage. It never installs dependencies, downloads models, applies migrations or processes household documents. Model metadata is not proof that inference works, and the base-table check is schema presence, not migration integrity.

nodes.label: ADR 0005 - The watched folder is polled, not subscribed to
nodes.community_name: ADR 0008 - Ingestion runs on a Celery worker
nodes.norm_label: adr 0005 - the watched folder is polled, not subscribed to
nodes.rationale: A filesystem event is the wrong signal: a file is created at the start of a copy, not the end, so anything built on watchdog events still has to debounce by watching the file stop changing - the event stream only decides how often we look. On Windows ReadDirectoryChangesW also drops events under buffer pressure, which would mean a document silently never filed. Adding a runtime dependency for one directory holding a handful of files a week also fails AGENTS.md rule 5.

nodes.label: ADR 0008 - Ingestion runs on a Celery worker
nodes.community_name: ADR 0008 - Ingestion runs on a Celery worker
nodes.norm_label: adr 0008 - ingestion runs on a celery worker
nodes.rationale: The whole pipeline ran on the thread that noticed the file, so a person dropping five scans watched the fifth wait forty seconds. Registration (one hash, one upsert) stays on the capture thread so the filed line appears immediately and the already-indexed check keeps saving work; reading moves behind the queue. Concurrency is one because Ollama is one endpoint in front of one graphics card - the queue buys a free watcher and restart survival, not parallelism, and the demonstration should not claim otherwise. No broker means inline, loudly, because a quiet fallback is the old stall with nobody knowing why.

nodes.label: ADR 0006 - pypdfium2 renders the quarantine page images
nodes.norm_label: adr 0006 - pypdfium2 renders the quarantine page images
nodes.rationale: Asking Docling for the page images would mean asking the component that could not read the document to prepare the evidence for the component that might, making the recovery rate a measurement of Docling twice. Shelling out to pdftoppm trades a declared dependency for an undeclared system one. pypdfium2 was already present transitively via Docling; declaring it directly is the point - code we call is a dependency we own, and a transitive dependency dropped in a minor release must break a lock file rather than break quarantine silently. 150 dpi is legible for 8pt print; four pages is a household document.

nodes.label: ADR 0009 - next-themes and lucide-react are the only two web dependencies beyond the stack
nodes.norm_label: adr 0009 - next-themes and lucide-react are the only two web dependencies beyond the stack
nodes.rationale: shadcn/ui is not a package but components copied in, several of which import things - so installing shadcn and installing nothing else are not the same act, and pretending otherwise puts undeclared packages in package.json under cover of a rule meant to prevent that. next-themes must write a class onto <html> before first paint or every load of a dark screen flashes white, which is a failure that shows up as a white flash rather than a test failure. clsx, tailwind-merge and cva are not on the list because shadcn's own init generates cn(). The larger cost this record makes visible: 'shadcn/ui' in AGENTS.md under-specifies the web lane.

nodes.label: ADR 0007 - The graph ships before retrieval and before a checkpoint table
nodes.community_name: ADR 0007 - The graph ships before retrieval and before a checkpoint table
nodes.norm_label: adr 0007 - the graph ships before retrieval and before a checkpoint table
nodes.rationale: Writing a retriever in core/retrieve/ would put two people's agents in the same directory in the same week and produce a second unmeasured baseline beside the one Lane B must publish. PostgresSaver creating its own tables at runtime would be rule 4 broken by a dependency rather than by a person, which is worse because nobody reviews it - so MemorySaver until a reviewed migration lands. Two follow-ups are owed: delete baseline.py when core/retrieve/ implements the ports, and migrate the checkpoint tables.

nodes.label: ADR 0010 - main is unprotected, and the discipline is human
nodes.norm_label: adr 0010 - main is unprotected, and the discipline is human
nodes.rationale: GitHub does not enforce rulesets on a private repository on a personal free plan, so a saved ruleset renders on the settings page and merges land unchecked anyway. This was not theoretical: two corpus commits landed directly on main, unreviewed, carrying a batch with no register - the precise class of problem CODEOWNERS was meant to route. A saved-but-inert ruleset is worse than an empty settings page because it tells the next person a gate exists. The task whose Done when can never become true is removed, because a permanent false red trains the team to ignore the board. The weekly integration pass is no longer a tidy-up; it is the only control.

nodes.label: Step 8 - switch a pack off
nodes.rationale: The platform argument as one gesture: reminders disappear, the documents are hidden from the vault, Ask abstains on a question it could answer a moment ago, and nothing is deleted. Nothing in the engine changed - the registry is read once per request and handed to the modules and to retrieval, neither of which knows a screen exists. A third subject appears because somebody dropped a YAML file in, not because anybody edited the interface.

nodes.label: Step 6 - the abstention
nodes.rationale: The step the demonstration exists for. Neither installed pack covers utilities, so asking for an electricity bill makes the abstention structural rather than lucky and it survives a corpus change. A system like this is useful not because it answers but because you can believe the answers, and you can only believe them if it is willing to say no. The headline evaluation number is the abstention rate on questions the corpus genuinely cannot answer.

nodes.label: Step 7 - the refusal to act
nodes.rationale: It refuses at the top of the graph, before retrieval runs - it did not go and look and then decline. Every pack manifest declares never_acts: true and the type system accepts no other value, so a pack that says otherwise does not load. A boundary that can be pointed at in the code rather than a promise about the model's judgement.

nodes.label: Step 2 - the source chip
nodes.rationale: Every row names the document and page it came from and pressing it shows that page, with the row still behind it - checking a claim does not cost you the claim. If the panel says the file is not in the inbox any more, that is correct honest behaviour, not a crash.

nodes.label: people and person_aliases
nodes.rationale: Two tables in db/migrations/0002_household.sql plus telegram_identities and document_attribution for provenance. An alias carries the literal string a document printed, its source (setup, model, user), whether it is confirmed, the generator's confidence and the document that raised the question. Attribution is the only ownership signal arriving before parsing - a payslip photographed on Rachel's phone is Rachel's whatever the OCR makes of the name - and a disagreement with extraction becomes a question rather than a silent overwrite.

nodes.label: Three buckets, not two
nodes.rationale: core/graph/scope.py partitions retrieved passages into mine (keep), someone else's (drop) and the household's, where subject IS NULL (keep). The third bucket is the one an implementation forgets: a home contents policy names nobody because it belongs to the address, and excluding it would break 'my home insurance' while looking like an empty vault. First-person detection is deliberately conservative - a relationship word or a non-owner's name leaves the question unscoped, because an over-eager filter fails as an absence rather than as an error.

nodes.label: The correctly-cited wrong person
nodes.rationale: The only failure mode in the architecture that citation does not defend against. Two term life policies differing only in whose name is on them both match; a cross-encoder has no representation of which human being a document is about, so it orders by textual relevance; the gate checks the sentence is supported by a retrieved chunk, and it is. The answer is delivered with a correct citation to the wrong person's policy and every check passes. The word 'my' had nothing to bind to.

nodes.label: Domain pack
nodes.rationale: The core platform knows nothing about tax or insurance - only how to ingest, search and answer with a citation. A pack is one YAML file that teaches it a subject, declaring document types and fields, a grounding corpus, capability-module registrations, a persona and guardrails. Since ADR 0017 document types and fields moved to core/documents.yaml and a pack holds only grounding, persona, guardrails, answering rules and advice.

nodes.label: The ten field types
nodes.rationale: string, identifier, person, money, integer, percent, date, month, enum, boolean. Each names its storage column (value_text, value_num, value_date) and its exact register format, so the spreadsheet and the database agree on what a value looks like. Pick by what the value is, not by how it is printed.

nodes.label: Pack grounding corpus
nodes.rationale: Authoritative reference material indexed beside the user's own documents. Never paraphrase a rule into it - index what the publisher wrote, because the moment you summarise the assistant cites your summary as though it were the publisher. Version by what the guidance applies to (iras_reliefs_ya2026, not iras_reliefs_september). Every file needs a sources.yaml provenance entry. A pack with no corpus is fine and sometimes correct.

nodes.label: Pack guardrails
nodes.rationale: must_cite (no claim without a document and page), abstain_below (the retrieval score under which the system says it does not know), never_acts (cannot be set to false - the type system rejects it), and the disclaimer rendered under every answer. Insurance sits at 0.45 and tax at 0.42 because a wrong answer about cover is worse than an unhelpful one. Regulatory framing belongs in the disclaimer, not the persona.

nodes.label: Pack persona is voice only
nodes.rationale: It cannot change retrieval, the score floor or the guardrails, so behaviour must not be smuggled into it. Two or three sentences on what the assistant does and, importantly, what it does not do.

nodes.label: Registering with capability modules
nodes.rationale: A pack declares reminder entries (from_field naming a date field, lead_days) and alert entries (metric, ceiling, warn_at) and gets reminders and alerts without writing any logic. Registering a module that is not installed is ignored rather than an error, so declaring a future module is safe.

nodes.label: Quarantine and the vision second pass
nodes.norm_label: quarantine and the vision second pass
nodes.rationale: A document the parser could not read queues rather than being dropped. --retry renders its pages and sends them to the vision-language model, which reads pixels rather than recovered text, then holds the result to the same pack schema and reports a recovery rate. Retry matches rows to files by SHA-256, so the original must still be in the inbox; a document whose file has left is offered as Forget it instead.

nodes.label: Ground truth Q&A test matrix
nodes.rationale: Ten questions paired with the exact answer and the document, page or clause that must be cited - including two designed to fail safely: the passport question that must abstain until the image exists, and the term life premium question that must disambiguate Marcus from Rachel per ADR 0011.

nodes.label: Derive the roster, then confirm it
nodes.norm_label: derive the roster, then confirm it
nodes.rationale: facts.subject is a printed string, so matching is about which strings a household's documents actually use, not about knowing who lives in the house. A person filling a first-run roster works from memory before any document is filed and produces something that looks complete and matches nothing - the worst state, because it is indistinguishable from a working one until an answer is wrong. So setup asks one question, everybody else arrives off a document, a person confirms, and only confirmed aliases scope anything. A wrong guess costs a tap, which is why the generator is allowed to guess.

nodes.label: facts.subject is never normalised
nodes.rationale: The alias table sits beside facts.subject and maps it; what the page said stays what the page said, so correcting the roster later cannot retroactively edit the record of what a document claimed. This mirrors the existing rule that identifier fields are stored verbatim. Matching is on lower(btrim(...)) only.

nodes.label: Five to eight fields per document type
nodes.norm_label: five to eight fields per document type

Every extra field is one the corpus owner fills in for hundreds of documents and one the extractor can get wrong, so breadth costs accuracy twice. required: false for fields a real document sometimes omits - a missing required field quarantines the whole document, which is right for a policy number and wrong for an optional excess.

nodes.label: identifier versus string
nodes.rationale: An identifier is matched exactly and never cleaned up - no spaces removed, no case changed - because MV-2026-448120 and mv2026448120 are different policies as far as a claim is concerned. This is the distinction that matters most among the ten types.

nodes.label: Scoping happens after retrieval, and that has a ceiling
nodes.community_name: ADR 0007 - The graph ships before retrieval and before a checkpoint table
nodes.norm_label: scoping happens after retrieval, and that has a ceiling
nodes.rationale: core/contracts.py was not touched (a household is not a pack and not a module) and neither was core/graph/ports.py, the contract with Lane B - which is why scoping happens after retrieval rather than as a SQL predicate. The measurable cost: a passage that did not survive the candidate cut cannot be scoped back in. With CANDIDATES = 40 over a household vault this is not currently reachable, but it is a real ceiling to hand to Lane B when hybrid search lands, because pushing the predicate into the query is a retrieval change and belongs with a retrieval measurement.

nodes.rationale: Extraction is a model call, not a pure function: temperature 0.0 with no seed is near-deterministic for one model and quantisation and is not guaranteed identical across GPUs and drivers. Two people can hold different facts rows for the same document, and only corpus/register/*.csv is the same on both machines - which is why evaluation never reads a live database for an expected answer. Record the models and quantisation too, because a different pull is a different vector space.
